Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version contains a short video that appears to demonstrate the Visual Intelligence feature on Apple's rumored AirPods with cameras. Let's take a look.

macOS 26.7 includes a demo video for AirPods with cameras

MacRumors discovered a short video in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to record the book he is reading, with Siri's voiceover stating:

The camera itself cannot be seen in the video; the earphone form factor is very similar to the current AirPods Pro. The most obvious difference is the stem, which appears slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris also posted the same video on X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch AirPods with cameras this year, internally codenamed B790. Earlier, MacRumors also found B790-related information in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, including code for 'image streaming'.

Interestingly, this batch of AirPods is reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model that Bloomberg said Apple has been developing under the internal codename B798, with the latter expected to launch in 2027.

Judging from Apple's decision to hide this demo in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to make their official debut at next month's iPhone launch event.

What are your thoughts on this video? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
